headline: Central Maine Medical Center fires or suspends 20 nurses amid union drive
dek: The Lewiston hospital says the employment actions followed documented policy and patient-care violations, while nurses and labor advocates say the discipline is retaliation for organizing.
body: Central Maine Medical Center has fired or suspended 20 nurses as employees prepare to vote on whether to unionize, escalating a dispute over staffing and patient care at the Lewiston hospital, according to Maine Public and local reporting.

At least 15 nurses had been fired and five remained suspended as of Friday, a hospital spokesperson told CentralMaine.com. The hospital said the actions were based on documented violations of established policies and standards, including alleged patient abandonment, timekeeping violations and conduct it said interfered with patient care or safety.

The Maine State Nurses Association and other labor advocates have characterized the discipline as retaliation for the organizing effort. Prime Healthcare, which owns CMMC through its nonprofit foundation, has denied targeting employees because of union activity and said its focus is patient safety and care-team support.
CMMC nurses filed for a union election in August and have raised concerns about staffing, equipment and basic supplies. The vote is scheduled for Sept. 24, according to CentralMaine.com.
author: NorthEast News Desk
